correctness.rationale: For each nonzero polynomial composition term P(h)h-prime, its top Laurent frequency is exactly (deg P+1)deg h; affine normalization of h removes two parameters, giving degree-d dimension at most 2d+2floor(n/d)-1. For intermediate 2<=d<=n-1, d+floor(n/d)<=n implies dimension <=2n-1. Degree-one h is equivalent by Chebyshev identities to a common odd-reflection phase and degree-n h to proportional coefficients; both have independent tangent dimension 2n+1. Their intersection has dimension n+2; at n=2 they exhaust all possibilities. An explicit complex Fourier coefficient test follows by phase elimination. Each assertion has an analytic argument; the supplementary exact-rational checker was run and passed without being substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The closest 2025/2026 complete paper identifies a composition criterion under its generic two-zero hypothesis but does not determine the Fourier-truncated semialgebraic dimension or the two maximal families. The 2024 first-harmonic predecessor establishes proportionality only at cutoff one. The present result adds the exact all-cutoff codimension, the distinct common-reflection branch at cutoff two, its intersection dimension, and a finite coefficient test. Pakovich (2017) gives trigonometric polynomial decomposition equivalences, while Briskin–Pakovich–Yomdin (2016) bounds polynomial Abel composition sets with fixed Q; both full texts were inspected and differ in mathematical object and parameters. The 2013 trigonometric Abel text was accessible only as abstract, leaving a residual comparison risk.
residual_risks: The full 2013 trigonometric Abel composition paper was not retrieved; its statements about the algebraic composition locus could overlap under a different differential equation.

The new claim is a geometric refinement of an existing common-factor characterization, not a first discovery of the criterion, of degree-one proportionality, or of the general Laurent decomposition formalism.

value.rationale: The exact codimension answers how exceptional global-center-producing composition coefficients are inside the natural finite Fourier parameter space. The two distinct maximal mechanisms disclose a structural phase change between first- and second-harmonic truncation, and the degree-two polynomial test is a complete coefficient-level classification not requiring ODE integration. This all-n exact invariant and natural low-degree classification are motivated by the established global-center composition criterion, not an arbitrary slice or a numerical improvement.
